sections.html:
Portland is Maine's largest city, built on a peninsula in Casco Bay. It borders South Portland, Westbrook and Falmouth, with about 21 square miles of land inside a much larger water boundary. The July 2025 estimate is 69,911 residents.

The peninsula and the mainland neighborhoods act like separate markets. The Old Port, Bayside, the Arts District, Munjoy Hill and the West End sit on or near the peninsula, and Deering covers the northern and eastern sections. Peaks, Great Diamond, Little Diamond, Cushing and Cliff islands belong to the city as well, with year-round ferry service from Casco Bay Lines.

Age and construction differ a lot between those areas. Portland burned badly in 1866, and buyers still ask about the age of peninsula buildings because of it. Deering was annexed in 1899 and has a different mix of housing, so comparable sales matter more than any citywide figure.

  • Ask for a full inspection history, since older masonry and wood-frame buildings can hide different problems.
  • Island properties carry ferry and utility questions a buyer will raise.
  • A short walk to a bus line or to the peninsula is worth a line in any listing, since it widens the pool of buyers who prefer not to drive daily.

Portland's ocean-moderated climate still brings snow, wind-driven rain and tidal flooding. Water is the longer-term concern: the 2024 record high tide reached 14.57 feet, and sea level is projected to rise roughly six inches by 2050 and two feet by 2060. A house near the waterfront, on a low street or on an island should expect flood zone and insurance questions from buyers and their lenders.

  • Check the FEMA flood map for your parcel before listing.
  • Ask your insurance agent for a flood quote so you can answer buyers.
  • Document sump pumps, drainage work and any past water in the basement.

sections.h2: How does Portland property tax work after the revaluation?
sections.html:
The 2025 revaluation raised values sharply and lowered the mil rate, so what you owe depends on how your own value moved. The city has about 19,400 residential properties and 1,920 commercial ones, with taxable real estate near $19.7 billion. After the 2021 revaluation the City Council voted to reassess every five years. Revaluations bring assessed values in line with the current market, as state law requires, and they shift the burden by value rather than raising total revenue.

Portland before and after the 2025 revaluation
MeasureBeforeFiscal 2026
Mil rate per $1,000$15.01$11.98
Median residential value$396,700$566,600

That is a 43 percent jump in the median residential value. Taxes are paid in two halves, one in the fall and one in March. The city's tax page shows the current year's dates. Maine's lien timeline runs from the commitment date, so a balance left open for months gets harder to deal with.

sections.h2: What if you owe property tax on a Portland house?
sections.html:
You can still sell with tax unpaid, because the payoff comes out of your proceeds at closing. Start by asking the city for a current balance, then give it to the title company so the closing statement shows it. Maine sets the lien steps in 36 M.R.S. section 942 and section 943. A demand notice can go out between 8 months and a year after commitment, and a lien that gets recorded ranks as a mortgage ahead of the others.

When tax, interest and costs stay unpaid for 18 months after filing, the lien is treated as foreclosed. The owner and any mortgage holders must be told 30 to 45 days before that date.

  • An application to fix an error or illegality in an assessment is due within 185 days of commitment, under section 841.
  • A hardship abatement on a primary residence can be requested within 3 years of commitment.
  • A seller who paid a pro rata share under a written proration agreement can ask the treasurer to record a certificate that says so.

Expect a transfer tax of $2.20 per $500 of value, with the buyer and the seller each paying half. From November 1, 2025, any transfer also owes $3.80 per $500 on the portion over $1 million, which makes early math worthwhile for owners of pricier peninsula homes.

Filing the deed costs $40 for most submitters, and a claimed exemption has to be written on the declaration of value form. Ask the title company to put these figures, along with your payoff and any unpaid tax, on a draft settlement statement a few days before you sign.

sections.h2: What to expect between offer and closing
sections.html:
Once you accept an offer, the title company searches the record for liens, confirms who owns the house and prepares a settlement statement. Your tax balance, mortgage payoff and half of the transfer tax come out of the price. The deed is recorded after closing.

Sellers who have the paperwork ready move fastest. Bring the deed, the mortgage statement, any lien notices and, for a rental, the tenant list with lease dates and your registration status. For a house near the water or on an island, have the flood map and insurance quote ready for the buyer's lender.

sections.h2: Rental registration rules for Portland owners
sections.html:
Residential rental units in Portland are registered every year, and short-term rentals carry a separate registration. The deadline is December 31, or thirty days after you start renting. Under Chapter 6 of the city code, a new owner or manager applies within 30 days of buying.

Both buyers and sellers feel this rule. Own a building with tenants? Check that your registration is current before listing, since a buyer's attorney will ask. Used the house for short-term rentals? Each listing needs your registration number, and registration allows on-site inspections. The city also has a Housing Safety and Rent Control office, and its code includes tenant protections.

A cash sale of a tenant-occupied house means you need not empty the building first, though Maine notice rules and lease terms still apply.

sections.h2: How can I sell a Portland house quickly?
sections.html:
Cash is the quickest way to close, while a listing can net more for a house in good shape. Portland's buyer demand helps a listing, but you still prepare the house, host showings and wait out a financing contingency. A cash buyer skips the repair requests and the appraisal.

  • Gather the deed, your mortgage payoff and any lien notices.
  • For a rental, note tenants, lease end dates and registration status.
  • Set the offer beside a listing's likely net after repairs, commission and months of holding costs.

Our written offers cover Portland houses in any condition, with no commission or fees to you. If the numbers do not work, you can walk away.

faqs.q: What is the Portland, Maine mil rate?
faqs.a: For fiscal 2026 it is $11.98 per $1,000 of assessed value, down from $15.01, after the city's revaluation. Check the City of Portland tax page for the current year.

faqs.q: When are Portland property taxes due?
faqs.a: Each year's bill is paid in two halves, one in the fall and one in March. Confirm the exact days with the city before choosing a closing date.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Portland house with a tax lien?
faqs.a: Yes. Closing proceeds pay the tax, interest and lien costs. Once 18 months pass after filing without redemption, a recorded lien is treated as foreclosed.

faqs.q: Who pays Maine transfer tax in Portland?
faqs.a: They split it evenly at $2.20 per $500 of value. Transfers from November 1, 2025 add $3.80 per $500 above $1 million.

faqs.q: Do I need to register a rental before selling in Portland?
faqs.a: Yes, registration is annual, due by December 31 or thirty days after renting begins. New owners apply within 30 days of buying, so a current registration smooths the sale.
